note: FOUNDRY'S OWN ADDITIONS TO THE MODEL LINEUP — rows Crucible has no manifest for.
model-lineup.json beside this file is Crucible's `foundry-lineup.json`, vendored
byte for byte so a keeper can compare it by content. It lists three models: the
page reader, the bf16 9B for narration cleanup, and the 4-bit 27B that Crucible
will serve translate/simplify/analysis with. Those are the models a CRUCIBLE
holds, and a Crucible is installed on a machine that can run them.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Foundry's local path is not a Crucible: it is Ollama, on
whatever card the person already owns, and Ollama's library carries the smaller
quantised Qwen tags that Crucible has no manifest for and never will. Dropping
them would mean the wizard on an 8 GB laptop offering exactly one model, 17.7 GB,
that the same screen then marks as bigger than the machine — which is the
opposite of what the wizard is for (Owen: *"foundry should work if they have no
idea what theyre doing"*). So they are KEPT, and kept HERE rather than merged
into the vendored file, because a hand-edited copy of a generated file is a copy
that silently loses the hand edits on the next re-vendor.
EVERY ID IN THIS FILE IS PREFIXED `foundry/`, so that a row of ours can never
collide with a Crucible manifest id — present or future. That is not decoration:
Crucible's `qwen3.5-9b` names the bf16 tag for cleanup, and this file's
`foundry/qwen3.5-9b` names the ordinary `qwen3.5:9b` for prose. Two different
models, one obvious name, and the prefix is what keeps them apart.
THE FLOOR. `minimumFor` on the 9B row is Owen's own rule — *"if their system
just isnt powerful enough for translation (smaller than 9b) then translation and
simplify is disabled"* (docs/SLOTS.md §1) — and it names translate and simplify,
which is what he named. Crucible's file declares its own floor at the 4-bit 27B;
llm-catalog.ts takes the SMALLEST declared floor, because the two catalogs are
answering different questions: Crucible's is what a Crucible will serve, and
this one is what an Ollama on this desk can actually be asked for.
Every `needsGB` here is `declared`: the download plus llm-catalog.ts's
OVERHEAD_GB, which is the arithmetic the old hand-written table used. Nothing in
this file has been measured, and a row Crucible later publishes a manifest for
should be DELETED from here rather than left to shadow it.

models.label: Qwen 3.5 · 0.8B
models.description: The smallest one. Runs on anything, including on the processor alone — use it when there is no GPU.

models.label: Qwen 3.5 · 2B
models.description: Small and quick. Fine for simplifying and for short passages; noticeably rougher on long translation.

models.label: Qwen 3.5 · 4B
models.description: The sweet spot for a laptop or an 8 GB card. Good prose, fast enough to watch.

models.label: Qwen 3.5 · 9B
models.description: Qwen 3.5's own default. Clearly better on long-form translation; wants a 12 GB card or more.

models.label: Qwen 3.5 9B · 8-bit
models.description: The narration cleanup's own default. Eight-bit weights, because the cleanup is a punctuation job rather than a prose job and the loss shows there first.

models.label: Qwen 3.5 · 27B
models.description: The 27B standard, in this generation. What a 24 GB card is for.

models.label: Qwen 3.5 9B · 16-bit (MLX)
models.description: The same weights at the same precision as Crucible's cleanup row, on ollama's MLX runner — the Apple Silicon spelling of the 16-bit row, and the only one that runs there.

models.label: Qwen 3.5 · 35B-A3B
models.description: Mixture-of-experts: 35B of weights, about 3B active per token, so it is faster than its size — but all 35B must be resident.

models.label: Qwen 3.5 · 122B-A10B
models.description: A workstation model. Listed so a machine that can run it is not quietly offered something smaller.
